title: Detection of Audio-Visual Content
summary: This detection strategy looks for synthetic audio and video content used to impersonate a real person, covering technique T1683.002. It matters because a convincing cloned voice or a face swapped video removes the last informal verification step that many organisations rely on, especially for payment approval and for help desk identity checks. The telemetry that makes it possible is meeting and call platform metadata, media file metadata including content provenance records, media analysis scores for lip synchronisation and compression artefacts, and the account and network context of the session. In practice the strategy fails because detection models are probabilistic, compressed or re-encoded media loses the artefacts they depend on, and low quality natural video triggers the same scores as a simple fake. Analysts therefore treat media analysis as one input and lean heavily on the process around the request, such as an unusual payment instruction or a sudden change of contact channel.

beginner.definition: Audio-visual content means sound and video. This detection looks for fake recordings or live deepfakes that copy a real person. It catches attempts to use a copied voice or face to gain trust.
beginner.whyItMatters: People trust a familiar voice or face more than an email. A fake recording can approve a payment or reset a password. The technology is now cheap and quick to use. Because the content is convincing, the strongest signals often come from the situation, not from the media itself.
howItWorks: You collect meeting and call records. These show who joined, when and from where.
You collect file metadata for recordings and voice notes. This shows how the file was made.
You run media analysis to look for unnatural lip movement or repeated image patterns.
You check the request in the call. A sudden payment or password request raises the score.
You check the account and device used. A new device or a first time caller stands out.
You combine the media score with the business context and route it for human verification.
beginner.example: Imagine a bank counter where a customer asks for a large withdrawal. The clerk knows the customer's face, so the request feels normal. But today the customer wears a very good mask and never removes it. He also refuses a personal question. The clerk should trust the missing answers, not the face. That is how deepfake detection works in practice.
takeaways: Media analysis is helpful but not decisive, so always weight the business context.
A sudden change of channel, such as an email that becomes a voice call, is a strong signal.
Out of band verification with a known number stops most voice cloning attacks.

objectives: Explain how voice cloning and face swapping undermine informal identity verification
Identify the call and meeting platform metadata that establishes who joined and from where
Interpret content provenance metadata in media files and state why it may be missing
Describe the media analysis signals used for synthetic detection and their false positive modes
Correlate a high risk media event with a payment, credential or access request in the same session
Define an out of band verification procedure that does not rely on the suspicious channel
dataSources: Video conferencing and voice call platform records including participant identity, join time, source address and call duration
Media file metadata for uploaded recordings and voice notes including producing application, bitrate history and content provenance manifest
Media analysis enrichment scores for lip synchronisation consistency, blink rate, spectral artefacts and frame duplication
Identity provider sign in logs recording the device, location and authentication method used during the session
Financial or service desk workflow records showing the payment, credential reset or access request raised during the session
logic: The pattern is a high impact request delivered through a rich media channel that is unusually hard to verify. You correlate the call or meeting record with the media analysis scores for any recording used, the device and location of the participant account, and the business transaction requested during or just after the session. The malicious case combines a first time or newly registered participant, a source address or device not previously used by that identity, media analysis flags for synthetic generation, and a request to change payment details, reset a credential or bypass a verification step. The benign case is a familiar participant on a known device with a normal request, even when compression artefacts produce an inconclusive media score. The process anomaly is more durable than the media score, because re-encoding removes artefacts but a fraudulently requested payment remains a fact.
pseudoQuery:
# title: Synthetic Media Indicators With High Impact Request in Call
# logsource:
#   product: windows
#   service: collaboration
# detection:
#   selection:
#     event_type: 'media_stream'
#     synthetic_score: > 0.85
#     participant_first_seen: true
#   selection_business:
#     request_type:
#       - 'payment_change'
#       - 'credential_reset'
#       - 'access_grant'
#   condition: selection or selection_business
# level: medium
falsePositives: Heavy video compression on poor home internet that makes lip movement look slightly out of step
Filters and beautification features in consumer video tools that alter facial geometry before streaming
Accessibility avatar or voice synthesis features used by employees with a documented speech or vision need
Conference recordings processed by transcription and noise reduction tools that resample the audio track
External candidates or suppliers joining from an unfamiliar device and location for a legitimate first meeting
tuningNotes: Set the alert to fire first on high impact requests from unverified participants, then use media scores only to raise severity rather than to trigger on their own, since compression noise produces many borderline scores. Baseline your own meeting platform's normal participant diversity so that first time external joiners do not dominate the queue. Allowlist accessibility avatar and speech synthesis accounts by identity rather than by media pattern. If you suppress all low quality media to reduce noise, you accept that a deliberately degraded deepfake will pass, so keep an alert on any payment or credential request that arrives through a media channel from an unverified participant.
